{
  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "For Time-to-Target: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor, followed by Welch's ANOVA if variance heterogeneity detected due to right-skewed distribution (max=201.39 vs mean=2.81)",
    "For Success: Binary logistic regression or generalized linear mixed model with binomial family rather than ANOVA, as Success is binary (0/1) violating normality and homoscedasticity assumptions; if ANOVA insisted upon, arcsine-square root transformation with caution",
    "For Path Efficiency: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm, with strong caution due to extreme right skew (max=29.82 vs mean=0.47); consider log-transformation or non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis as primary analysis",
    "For Average Speed: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm, with attention to right tail (max=75.35 vs mean=12.50); Welch's ANOVA or robust methods if variance inequality across paradigms",
    "For AD (Angular Dispersion): One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm, noting bounded [0,1] range; check for floor/ceiling effects and consider beta regression or arcsine transformation if variance near boundaries differs"
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Violated by repeated measures within 8 mice; current analysis ignores nesting—mixed-effects models with Mouse as random intercept are required for valid inference",
    "Normality: Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests for residuals; expected failures for Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, and Average Speed due to right skew; Success inherently non-normal",
    "Homoscedasticity: Levene's test across paradigms; expected violation given scale differences between Combined (n=48846) and smaller groups like Bright Visual Only (n=3323)",
    "Sample size imbalance: Extreme imbalance (Combined 63.7% of data vs Bright Visual Only 4.3%) affects Type I error rates and power; Welch correction or weighted procedures needed",
    "Outliers: Extreme values in Time-to-Target (max=201.39), Path Efficiency (max=29.82), and Average Speed (max=75.35) require inspection; winsorization or robust methods may be necessary"
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If omnibus test significant for continuous variables: Games-Howell post-hoc for unequal variances and sample sizes, or Tukey-Kramer with Welch correction",
    "Pairwise comparisons focus: Combined vs all single-modality paradigms (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) to assess multimodal enhancement; all stimulation vs Sham for efficacy",
    "Effect sizes: Cohen's d or Hedges' g with confidence intervals for all pairwise comparisons, accounting for unequal sample sizes",
    "For Success (if logistic framework): Odds ratios with 95% CI for each paradigm relative to Sham reference, with multiplicity correction (Benjamini-Hochberg FDR)",
    "Multiplicity control: False discovery rate control across 5 paradigms × 4 continuous variables = 20 comparisons; family-wise error rate for planned contrasts"
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Combined paradigm likely shows superior performance (lower Time-to-Target, higher Success, higher Path Efficiency, higher Average Speed, lower AD) compared to unimodal paradigms based on typical multisensory integration effects, though this is speculative without data access",
    "ICMS Only may show intermediate performance between Combined and Sham, with substantial uncertainty given smaller sample size (n=11378 vs 48846)",
    "Visual paradigms (Dim vs Bright) may differ in path efficiency and angular dispersion due to visibility constraints; Bright Visual Only potentially outperforming Dim Visual Only",
    "Sham expected to show poorest performance across metrics, serving as baseline for effect size quantification",
    "Large sample for Combined (n=48846) will drive statistical significance; practical significance requires effect size interpretation",
    "AD (angular dispersion) expected to inversely correlate with Path Efficiency and Success, with lowest values in Combined condition if multisensory integration improves heading stability"
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Pseudoreplication: 76655 trials from 8 mice violate independence assumption; standard ANOVA p-values anti-conservative; mixed-effects models essential for valid inference",
    "Extreme sample imbalance: Combined paradigm dominates (63.7%), reducing precision for comparisons involving smaller groups and potentially biasing variance estimates",
    "Missing covariates: No trial-level information on learning effects, session, or task difficulty; temporal autocorrelation unaddressed",
    "Success as binary: Standard ANOVA inappropriate; analysis plan specifies alternative but this complicates cross-variable synthesis",
    "Single summary view: 'summary_only' data view provides no distributional detail within paradigms; cannot assess bimodality or mixture distributions that may affect inference",
    "No interaction assessment: Cannot evaluate whether effects differ by mouse or vary with task experience",
    "Temperature=0.0 and deterministic prompting: Analysis reproducible but may miss model uncertainty in interpretation; no ensemble of analytical perspectives"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) for continuous outcomes and generalized linear mixed models (GLMMs) with binomial family for Success, with Mouse as random intercept and Stim Paradigm as fixed effect; include planned contrasts with multiplicity correction; conduct sensitivity analyses with (a) exclusion of extreme outliers, (b) log-transformation for right-skewed variables, and (c) non-parametric permutation tests to validate parametric findings; finally, compute intra-class correlation (ICC) to quantify mouse-level variance contribution and guide experimental design for future studies."
}
